newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO reports bridge blown up in northeast Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO reports bridge blown up in northeast Bosnia.

text.p: An explosion damaged a bridge near a former front line in northeast Bosnia over the weekend, the NATO-led peace force said on Sunday.
The blast was heard late on Saturday in the village of Celic just inside Bosnia's Serb republic near the boundary of the Moslem-Croat federation, the Stabilisation Force (SFOR) said in a statement.

It was unclear what type of explosive was used but a three-foot section of electric detonation wire was found at the site, SFOR said. A brick pillar holding up the east side of the bridge was damaged, making it impossible for cars to pass.
Tensions have been running high along the former front line in northeast Bosnia where Moslems want to move back to villages in territory controlled by Bosnian Serbs.
About 150 Bosnians have won permission to move back to their homes in the nearby village of Gajevi later this week and would have passed over the bridge to reach the village.
In November, a Moslem was killed and two Serbs were wounded in Gajevi when a firefight erupted after angry Serbs tried to prevent Moslems returning.
Both sides had carried arms into the demilitarised "Zone of Separation" in violation of rules enforced by SFOR.

Moslems say the Dayton peace agreement guarantees refugees the right to return to their homes. But Bosnian Serb police view this as intrusion in Serb territory, which was purged of Moslem and Croats during the Bosnian war.
